newsitem.title: UK: Gazprom to choose ABN, Goldman to raise $1 bln - FT.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom to choose ABN, Goldman to raise $1 bln - FT.

text.p: Russian natural gas producer Gazprom is set to confirm it has appointed bankers ABN AMRO Holding NV and Goldman Sachs to raise $1 billion to help pay a huge tax bill, the Financial Times newspaper said on Wednesday.
Gazprom subsidiaries owe 15 trillion roubles ($2.6 billion) in unpaid taxes and the newspaper said the appointment reflected a struggle among Gazprom's directors over future financing strategy.
ABN and Goldman Sachs would be chosen above investment banks Dresdner Kleinwort Benson and Morgan Stanley, which have advised Gazprom on other matters.
The Financial Times said some bankers feared the appointment of multiple advisers could derail the capital-raising programme and discredit Russian borrowers in the eyes of foreign investors.
"There is such a division of interests within the company that it is almost paralysed," one banker close to Gazprom told the newspaper.
Gazprom was likely to opt for a $1 billion bridging loan to be refinanced at a later date through a syndicated bank loan, the paper said.
Gazprom has enormous natural resources but needs funds to build pipelines and pay off debt.

Russia accounts for a third of the world's gas reserves and 27 percent of its output. Gazprom accounts for about 95 percent of Russian output and is a key supplier to the Western European natural gas market. ($ = 5748 Russian Roubles)
